Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. The application stands disposed of.

3. The present petition has been filed seeking quashing of FIR No. 543/2016 under Sections 406/498A/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC) registered at Police Station Amar Colony on the ground of settlement.
4. The petitioner no.1 is the husband of the respondent no.2 and the petitioners no.2, 3 and 4 are family members of the petitioner no.1.
The marriage of the petitioner no.1 and the respondent no.2 was solemnized on 10th December, 2012 according to Hindu rites and ceremonies.
One minor

sentences.text: Subsequently, the parties have settled their disputes in terms of Deed of Settlement dated 15th April, 2023 entered into between the parties, annexed as Annexure C to the petition.
The parties have also been granted divorce by mutual consent vide decree dated 9th August, 2023.
7. As per the settlement, a sum of Rs.21,00,000/- was payable to the respondent no.2.
Out of the aforesaid amount, a sum of Rs.16,00,000/- has already been paid.

The petitioners have brought a demand draft of Rs.5,00,000/- in Court today and the same has been handed over to the respondent no.2.
8.
Issue notice.

9. Notice is accepted by the learned APP appearing on behalf of the State and by the counsel appearing on behalf of the respondent no. 2.
10.
The respondent no.2 is present in Court and has been identified by her counsel and by the Investigating Officer (IO).
She informs the Court that she has settled the matter of her own free will and without any coercion.
She further states that she has no objection to quashing of the FIR.
11. The petitioners are also present in Court and have been identified by their counsel.
They affirm the statement of the respondent no.2 and undertake to abide by the terms of settlement arrived at between the parties.

12. Considering the above settlement between the parties and the chances of conviction of the petitioners being remote and bleak, there is no use continuing with proceedings of the present FIR as it would be a misuse of This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 18/09/2023 at 22:51:53 the process of the Court and an unnecessary burden on the State exchequer.
Hence, it would be in the interest of justice to quash the aforementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
13. There is one minor child born from the wedlock, who is in the care and custody of the respondent no.2/mother.
It is directed that the settlement executed between the petitioners and respondent no.2 as well as this order shall have no effect on the rights of the minor child in the future.
14. Consequently, FIR No. 543/2016 registered at Police Station Amar Colony and proceedings pursuant thereto are quashed.
15. The petition stands disposed of.
